messages.content:
You label USMLE-style questions for a psychiatry benchmark whose only knowledge source is the DSM-5 manual.

Fields:
- psychiatry: true if the question mainly tests psychiatric or behavioral knowledge: mental disorders and their
  diagnosis, criteria, course or differential; psychopharmacology; substance intoxication, withdrawal or use
  disorders; sleep, eating and neurocognitive disorders; psychotherapy; defense mechanisms; suicide risk.
  False when psychiatric words are incidental (e.g. "ST depression" on an ECG, an anxious patient whose
  problem is surgical, a question about a drug's cardiac side effect).
- dsm_answerable: true if DSM-5 text (diagnostic criteria, features, duration, prevalence, course, differential
  diagnosis) is enough to pick the correct option; false if it needs drug choice, mechanisms, pharmacology,
  management steps, ethics, or lab interpretation.
- category: one of diagnosis, criteria_duration, differential, treatment_pharmacology, management_ethics,
  substance, other.

Respond with only a JSON object:
{"psychiatry": true or false, "dsm_answerable": true or false, "category": "...", "reason": "one short sentence"}

Question:
A 21-year-old man comes to the physician because of nervousness and difficulty sleeping over the past 2 weeks. Three months ago, he started a new team project at his job. He says that he has trouble falling asleep at night because he thinks about the project. He insists on checking the work of his teammates and spends several hours each week making elaborate lists and schedules. He refuses to let others take on more tasks because he thinks that only he can complete them satisfactorily. The project deadline has already been postponed once. He says, “My teammates never understand how important it is to do things the right way.” Ever since high school, he has used the majority of his time to plan out assignments and does not have time to regularly participate in social activities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

Options:
A. Obsessive-compulsive personality disorder
B. Obsessive-compulsive disorder
C. Generalized anxiety disorder
D. Schizoid personality disorder
E. Adjustment disorder with mixed anxiety and depressed mood
"

Correct answer: A. Obsessive-compulsive personality disorder

text: {"psychiatry": true, "dsm_answerable": true, "category": "diagnosis", "reason": "Tests DSM-5 diagnostic criteria for obsessive-compulsive personality disorder (perfectionism, reluctance to delegate, overdevotion to work since early adulthood) versus OCD, GAD, and adjustment disorder."}
